The receiving client and default settings are not documented.

claims.answer: User grants directories, network/credential/repo access and temporary tunnels. Approvals come from the operator in the thread; relayed approvals record the user's instruction, and vault access must be approved by the user directly. Approver roles are not further defined. Agents see no folder until it is explicitly trusted: the site says the rest of the machine is "invisible", and the CLI README says Linzumi only edits inside trusted folders. The bootstrap agent adds /tmp/hello_linzumi to the trust list on first run, and linzumi connect also trusts its selected --cwd for that runner process. The home-page Trust section says permissions expire with the session (re-grant explicitly to extend) and forwarded ports close when the thread ends. No manual revoke control is documented in the checked site, walkthrough and CLI README.

sources.title: Linzumi product and pricing
sources.finding: macOS Apple Silicon beta and browser workspace. Multiple humans steer concurrent local agents in one thread; inline diffs, replay, previews and exportable artifacts. Personal free solo plan; Company $100/month flat; Enterprise offers SSO/SAML/SCIM and self-hosting.

sources.title: Linzumi Commander CLI README
sources.locator: Try it; Manual Runner Setup; headless auth; MCP; working as a team
sources.finding: Official @linzumi/cli README documents trusted project folders, browser/local separation, Codex launch, headless VPS device-flow authentication, scoped MCP message/thread/channel reads and owner DM; team members can steer and interrupt the same thread.

sources.title: Linzumi CLI release and recovery notes
sources.finding: Latest package 1.0.335 published 2026-11-07. Saved replies recover only after receipt/ownership/archive checks; Ready waits for all recovery obligations. File uploads permit registered Git task worktrees and reject symlink/hidden/unrelated-path escapes.

sources.title: Linzumi C3 roadmap
sources.finding: C3 cited answers, live call transcription, contradiction reconciliation and context-derived verifiable specs are marked Coming soon. No release date stated.

sources.title: Commander native coding engines
sources.locator: npm tarball digest, no gitHead; bundled/minified implementation; VY native execution list; rre SDK loader; SDK query spawn; Bye/zj auth probes
sources.finding: The execution selector admits Codex and Claude Code. The Claude path imports @anthropic-ai/claude-agent-sdk, calls its query with the Claude executable and native settingSources, and accepts native OAuth credentials or provider API keys. The Codex auth path reads the native auth.json OAuth account or OPENAI_API_KEY. Other MCP client configuration formats do not launch additional engines. Inspected the exact published 1.0.340 package, pinned by its npm SHA512 integrity digest rather than a Git revision.

sources.title: Commander independent project issue graph
sources.locator: npm tarball digest, no gitHead; bundled/minified implementation; linzumi_get/create/update_project_task; dependency tools; start_coding_job project_task_id
sources.finding: Registered live MCP handlers create durable project issue/group records with todo/active/blocked/review/done/canceled statuses, descriptions, assignees, priorities and dependency edges. Creation does not start a coding job; explicit start_coding_job binds project_task_id and transitions todo to active. This is native backlog storage separate from coding-session lifecycle. Inspected the exact published 1.0.340 package, pinned by its npm SHA512 integrity digest rather than a Git revision.

sources.title: Commander product-supplied child-job coordinator
sources.locator: npm tarball digest, no gitHead; bundled/minified implementation; linzumi_spawn_child_job; discover_coding_jobs; send_coding_job_message; scoped handler adapters
sources.finding: The product supplies a coding-job coordinator tool that instructs its agent to plan a DAG, spawn durable child jobs under its own job on selected harnesses/models, discover job reports and message workers. Registered handlers dispatch through scoped Linzumi APIs; this is not merely a third-party harness subagent display. Inspected the exact published 1.0.340 package, pinned by its npm SHA512 integrity digest rather than a Git revision.

sources.title: Commander unattended topic checks and wakes
sources.locator: npm tarball digest, no gitHead; bundled/minified implementation; create_topic_wake_subscription; create_topic_check; update/resume subscription handlers
sources.finding: The shipped handlers create standing subscriptions that wake @linzumi when topic entries arrive and scheduled checks that run an argv command on the workspace agent runner. Delivery supports debounce/windows, failure pause and explicit resume. Signed incoming webhook events can feed topics. This is product-owned unattended event/schedule configuration, requiring the associated runner. Inspected the exact published 1.0.340 package, pinned by its npm SHA512 integrity digest rather than a Git revision.

sources.title: Commander PR workflow metadata
sources.locator: npm tarball digest, no gitHead; bundled/minified implementation; linzumi_link_coding_job_pull_request registered handler
sources.finding: The native handler links the active job to a GitHub repository/PR number and URL, stores head/base branches and SHAs, and feeds PR comments, files, commits, checks, deployments and reviews into the job workflow metadata view. This establishes management of an existing PR; it does not claim a native PR-creation command. Inspected the exact published 1.0.340 package, pinned by its npm SHA512 integrity digest rather than a Git revision.

sources.title: Commander package license metadata
sources.finding: The first-party published Commander client package declares MIT. The package does not include a license grant or source distribution for the main hosted Linzumi chat/control-plane service; its client license cannot establish the product-level hosted-core license.

sources.title: Linzumi home and pricing
sources.locator: Hero; Trust & control; Pricing (Personal, Company, Enterprise)
sources.finding: Beta macOS app for Apple Silicon plus web signup. Personal free for one person with unlimited channels, own keys and machine; Company $100/month flat for the whole team, no per-seat pricing, unlimited agent-hours, shared channels, priority support, first month free, cancel anytime; Enterprise quote with SSO/SAML, SCIM, self-hosting/VPC/own cloud, SOC 2, audit logs, SLA. Every plan runs agents on hardware the customer controls with its own credentials. Staff can read only #linzumi-support; agents see only explicitly approved directories; forwarded ports close with the thread; permissions expire with the session; network egress, credential reads and repo writes gate on operator approval.

sources.title: What is Linzumi?
sources.finding: Marketing walkthrough: sign up in the browser, connect a laptop, dev box or server, open a channel per project, service or bug. A channel shows the searchable thread, live terminal/logs/file tree, a tunneled preview with in-place comments and an ordered replay of agent actions. Team members steer, hand off mid-task and approve in the thread; the agent merges and posts deploy links in the example. Agents inherit the machine environment and secrets, watch and restart service processes, page a human with context, and run recurring channel jobs. Works from any browser or device.

sources.title: Linzumi Commander CLI 1.0.350 README
sources.locator: Intro; Why a CLI; Working as a team; Trusted folders; When something looks wrong
sources.finding: Package 1.0.350 published 2026-11-21 (MIT). Agents run on the local machine with real env vars and branches; chat runs in the browser and reaches users in the browser or on the phone. Linzumi edits only inside explicitly trusted folders. If the browser says no runner is connected, the Commander terminal must still be open.

sources.title: Commander 1.0.350 MCP tool registrations
sources.locator: npm tarball, no gitHead; bundled implementation; registerTool calls for linzumi_ask_user_question/update_needs_you, linzumi_set_generated_notification_decision, linzumi_resolve_permission_request, linzumi_set_job_permission_mode, linzumi_get_vault_values, linzumi_dev_service_start, linzumi_search_workspace, linzumi_get_thread_transcript, linzumi_read_terminal_screen, linzumi_link_coding_job_pull_request
sources.finding: Registered tools let a job raise a needs-you question to one named member with urgency (urgent re-pushes every 3 hours outside quiet hours; workspace-gated), move it to another addressee, and toggle the workspace push-notification decision flag. Permission modes are ask, auto_approve (sandboxed, answered on the record) and bypass_all; vault secret access needs the user's own thread-scoped approval and is never auto-approved; relayed approvals record the user's instruction. Managed dev services survive the turn, auto-restart on crash and health-probe declared ports. Workspace search is hybrid lexical+semantic with permalinks; full thread transcripts include commands and file changes; terminal sessions can be opened, read and sent input; jobs link a GitHub PR whose comments, checks and deployments feed job metadata.

sources.title: Commander 1.0.350 generated notification decision tool
sources.finding: The tool turns the workspace flag generated_notification_decision on or off exactly as its Developer-tab switch does; when on, push notifications in the workspace are decided by the generated notification decision. It is refused (forbidden) unless the asker is a developer and a member of the workspace.

sources.title: Commander 1.0.350 needs-you availability refusal
sources.finding: Needs-you calls can return not_available_yet with the message "needs-you items are not turned on for this workspace", telling the job to wait or say what it needs in the thread. Needs-you items are therefore available only in workspaces where they have been turned on.

sources.title: Linzumi Commander CLI 1.0.350 README
sources.locator: Trusted folders; What is new (task worktree uploads)
sources.finding: Linzumi only edits inside folders the user has explicitly trusted; the trust list lives at ~/.linzumi/config.json. The bootstrap agent adds /tmp/hello_linzumi on first run, and for linzumi connect the selected --cwd is also trusted for that runner process. Coding agents can generate files in Linzumi task worktrees at ~/.linzumi/worktrees/<repository>/<task>, which Git must register as worktrees of the trusted repository.

sources.title: Linzumi home: Trust & control and Pricing
sources.locator: Trust & control ("Agents only see what you let them see"; "Tunnels close when the conversation does"; "Permissions expire with the session"); Pricing, Company plan list
sources.finding: The Trust section says to approve directories explicitly and that the rest of the machine is "invisible, period"; forwarded ports are scoped to the thread and ending the thread ends access; capabilities do not persist and must be re-granted explicitly to extend. No manual revoke control is described. The Company plan lists "Run services and host what you build" without saying where services run.
